skills.title: Assess before deleting
skills.description: Remove a file, branch, worktree, record or process only after each candidate has been classified by what depends on it and what would be lost, and the reversible step has been taken first.
inputs: the candidates for removal, each named by its path, ref, record id or process id
a checkout with git history, the peer board and the repository's own diagnostics
outputs: a removal table naming each candidate, its class, the evidence behind the class, its risk and the action taken
a rescue ref or pushed branch for anything that held work not reachable elsewhere
the verification that ran after the removal, with its exit codes

examples.title: Remove worktrees that look finished
examples.body:
The disk is filling and several linked worktrees belong to branches that were merged. Each
one is a candidate, not a decision: a merged branch can still hold uncommitted work.

```text
Apply the assess-before-deleting skill to every linked worktree whose branch is merged into
master. Classify each with git status, the unpushed commits and the peer board; push or
rescue anything that holds work, remove only the low-risk ones, then run majordomus doctor.
```

skills.title: Deploy the site by hand
skills.description: Publish the website to GitHub Pages from a terminal, through the one script the Pages workflow runs, when waiting for the Actions queue is not acceptable.
inputs: the commit to publish, checked out with a clean tree and contained in origin/master
zola, node_modules (npm ci) and, for the full gate, cargo; or, without cargo, the rustdoc, ui-snapshot and cockpit-snapshot artifacts of the same commit's Pages run
the operator's word, in this session, that the site is to go live now
outputs: a gh-pages commit naming the source commit, or a refusal naming the gate that stopped it
the real-browser probe's verdict over the live homepage, with its screenshot and result.json
a checkpoint recording the deploy and the commit it published

skills.title: Evolve the repository's know-how
skills.description: Turn what sessions observed into reviewed knowledge and into the rule, skill, document or test each lesson belongs in, then deliver the change and tell every peer what moved.
inputs: a checkout on a branch of its own, with the tool's task open and its scope naming the knowledge section
the candidates awaiting review, and whatever this session met and has not yet recorded
what the providers' memories and the peers' announcements and handovers hold since the last evolve, read as data
outputs: every reviewed candidate promoted with its evidence or rejected with its reason
for each promoted lesson that asks for one, the change to the rule, skill, document or test it belongs in
a delivered change, and an announcement and a handover that name what moved

examples.title: After an incident
examples.body:
A commit stood fourteen minutes behind another worktree's build lock, and the cause was
found. Evolve from it: record the observation against the rule that should have caught it,
derive and promote the lesson with the measurement as its evidence, add the shape to the
gate and the case that proves the gate refuses it, write the post-mortem as a curated note,
amend the decision whose accepted cost this was, deliver, and tell the board which builds
are bounded now and what to export until the change lands.

skills.title: Implement a change
skills.description: Carry a requested change through the repository evidence-first, from the invariant it must keep to a verified, reconciled, documented and committed tree, without widening its scope.
inputs: the requested change, in the requester's words, with any issue or specification it names
a checkout with git history and the effective context for every path the change will touch
the repository's verification, generation and drift-check commands
outputs: the change, as coherent commits whose messages name what each proves
behavioural evidence that distinguishes the new behaviour from the old
regenerated projections and a clean drift check
an implementation record naming the invariant, the evidence, what was reconciled and what remains unsupported

examples.title: Add a declarative catalogue item
examples.body:
```text
Apply the implement skill to add a use case under .ai/repo/use-cases/. Touch canonical
data only; then validate, regenerate, and prove that the command line, MCP and the site
show the new item with no code or registry edited; finish with the drift checks.
```

Expected shape: modify canonical data only → validate → regenerate → prove propagation
through every surface → drift check clean.

examples.title: Fix a defect
examples.body:
```text
Apply the implement skill to the defect "finish accepts a completed outcome while an
open question names the task". Reproduce it with a case under test/cases/ that fails
today, make the smallest fix, show the case passing, and review the adjacent gates for
the same shape of hole.
```

Expected shape: reproduce → regression evidence → smallest fix → the original failure
no longer occurs → adjacent regression surface reviewed.

examples.title: Implement a feature from an issue
examples.body:
```text
Apply the implement skill to issue I0042 (majordomus plan show I0042).
Scope: the paths the issue declares. Before the mechanism: the invariant, the observable
behaviour and the test that proves it. After: generate, generate-site-data, both --check,
doctor; then plan evidence and plan done with the case that proves each criterion.
```

Expected shape: inspect → invariant → observable behaviour → behavioural test →
implementation → diagnostics and documentation → verify → commit → report.

examples.title: Make an operation faster
examples.body:
```text
Apply the implement skill to make `majordomus doctor` finish under its budget.
Record the baseline (MJ_TIMING=1 majordomus doctor, majordomus bench), find the phase
that dominates, change it, compare against the baseline, and add a regression guard only
where the contract justifies one.
```

Expected shape: baseline → bottleneck identified → change → comparison → regression
guard where justified.

examples.title: Refactor a subsystem without changing its behaviour
examples.body:
```text
Apply the implement skill to refactor lib/knowledge.sh so that discovery is one function.
First write down the observable behaviour that must be preserved and the cases that pin
it; run them before and after; prove equivalence with the same outputs byte for byte.
```

Expected shape: preserved observable behaviour stated → tests before → refactor →
tests after → equivalence shown.

skills.title: Take finished work to a verified master
skills.description: Carry a finished change from an open pull request to master and beyond through the one integration engine and the one landing seat, answering at each stage why it is not there yet and stopping only at a landing verified on master, a release, or a named blocker with its next act.
inputs: the work to integrate: one pull request, a train, or every open pull request
the last recorded forge observation and the audit trail of this checkout's executor
the peer board, with who holds `seat/landing` and `seat/release`
outputs: for each pull request, the stage it reached (open, ready, landed, released, deployed) with the evidence of each
the landing verified on master by commit, or the blocker that stopped it, its owner and the next act
the measurements of the attempt (wait, check time, retries), read from the engine, never estimated

examples.title: Finished, but not on master
examples.body:
The implementation was pushed yesterday and its pull request is open with a green check.
Find out why it is not on master and carry it there: read its disposition and the evidence
behind it, see who holds the landing seat, make the head ready (contains master, required
check passed on that head, issue evidence recorded), announce it to the seat with its sha,
and verify the landing afterwards — the head an ancestor of master, master's own run on that
commit green, then whether the release seat has released it. Report each stage reached with
its run or commit, and the blocker with its owner where it stopped.

skills.title: Pack the sources for a ChatGPT project
skills.description: Turn a committed tree into token-bounded Markdown shards that a ChatGPT project's file search indexes, verified to carry no binary, worktree, link, build output, projection or leaked value, and hand them over with the commit they were cut from.
inputs: a committed tree at the revision the conversation is about
the question the ChatGPT conversation is meant to answer
outputs: a verified pack directory under tmp/packs/ holding 00-INDEX.md, the shards and pack.json
the upload list, the commit, the token total and what the profile left out

examples.title: Upload the sources to a ChatGPT project
examples.body:
A design question is to be discussed in the operator's ChatGPT project, which must see the
current sources and nothing else.

```text
Apply the pack-for-chatgpt skill: commit the change, plan the chatgpt profile and read what
it leaves out, build the pack, confirm the verifier is clean, and report the commit, the
files to upload and the token total.
```

skills.title: Pack the repository for an outside reviewer
skills.description: Prepare a bounded, reproducible snapshot of the tracked tree for a reviewer who cannot read the repository directly, with the local half and anything secret left out and the questions the review must answer written down.
inputs: the question the outside review must answer, and the paths it concerns
a committed tree at the revision to be reviewed
outputs: an archive of the tracked tree at a named commit, with its file list and size
a brief for the reviewer naming the commit, the scope, the questions and what was left out

examples.title: A second opinion from a model without the checkout
examples.body:
A design change should be reviewed by a model in another tool that cannot read the
repository.

```text
Apply the pack-for-review skill: commit the change, take the context profile of majordomus
archive at that commit, read the dry run for anything that must not leave, and write a brief
naming the commit, the question and what the pack leaves out.
```

skills.title: Project picture
skills.description: Build the best evidenced picture of a project from every source the worker can reach, local first, every source optional, with each claim tagged and sourced and every gap recorded.
inputs: PROJECT: a repository, a set of repositories, or a name to resolve (default: the repository of the working directory)
SCOPE: paths or repositories to narrow to (default: all of PROJECT)
MODE: auto | local | global | offline (default: auto, detected, never asked)
BUDGET: wall-clock seconds and tokens for the whole run (default: 600 s; per source a tenth of it)
SINCE: the time window for activity (default: 30 days; history before it is summarised)
DEPTH: quick | standard | deep (default: standard)
outputs: the picture in Markdown, sections as in Output
the same picture as JSON with the same structure
a coverage ledger with one row per source tier and adapter
proposed records (knowledge candidates, questions, a handover body), written only when asked

examples.title: Picture across every project on a machine
examples.body:
Intent: "What is going on across all my projects?" There is no repository in the working
directory, or PROJECT names several. MODE auto resolves to global.

The worker enumerates repositories under the workspace root (any directory that `git
rev-parse` accepts, plus the linked worktrees), and records which are supervised. It runs
stages 2–8 per repository within an equal share of BUDGET, with DEPTH quick unless one is
named, and then merges the results:

- one TL;DR line and one coverage row per repository;
- the links between repositories: shared remotes, a dependency named in a manifest, the same
  tracker project, the same people on the board;
- shared resources that one project's state depends on, such as a CI slot cap or a request
  budget per consumer, as DERIVED findings;
- the cross-project next actions, ranked by what they unblock.

Confidentiality is applied per repository. A finding from one project's external channel
never appears in another project's section.

examples.title: Picture with no network
examples.body:
Intent: "Give me the picture of acme-ledger, offline." MODE offline, or MODE auto on a machine
whose remotes do not answer.

The worker runs stages 1–5 and 10 only. `git fetch` fails, so trunk is read as the last
fetched `origin/main`, and the picture says how old that fetch is. Stage 10 still reconciles
the tree against the `.ai/` records and derives plan drift from local data. Nothing from the
forge, the tracker or the conversations appears as a fact.

The coverage ledger is what makes the result honest:

```markdown
| Tier | Adapter | State | Elapsed | Locators | Newest | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T0 | git | partial | 5 s | 28 | 2031-03-11 | fetch failed; origin/main as of last fetch 2031-03-11T09:02Z |
| T1 | majordomus | read | 19 s | 15 | 2031-03-10 | context, plan, knowledge, decisions |
| T2 | forge CLI | skipped | 0 s | 0 | – | offline |
| T3 | tracker | skipped | 0 s | 0 | – | offline |
| T4 | chat workspace | skipped | 0 s | 0 | – | offline |
| T5 | mesh, other checkouts | partial | 3 s | 4 | 2031-03-11 | local worktrees only |
```

Next actions that would need a remote source say so, for example: "confirm PR #31's state
when online".

examples.title: Picture of one supervised project, every source reachable
examples.body:
Intent: "Load everything about acme-ledger and give me the picture." MODE auto resolves to
local and supervised, DEPTH standard, SINCE 30 days.

The worker runs stages 1–5 before any network call. It then gives the forge, the tracker and
the chat workspace one read-only worker each, and reconciles their results in stage 10.

Excerpt of the Markdown output:

```markdown
## TL;DR (as_of 2031-03-14)
- acme-ledger reconciles supplier invoices read from scanned documents.
- Trunk has the matching engine; operation still runs the version before it.
- Blocker: deploys from trunk fail since 2031-03-03 (approval guard, run 812).
- Next: a second reviewer approves PR #23; owner: the infrastructure lead.
- Scope agreed in chat on 2031-03-12 is not in the plan yet.

## Contradictions
| One side | Other side | Locator |
|---|---|---|
| plan: T7.2 todo (DERIVED from plan.json) | PR #31 merged, closes it (OBSERVED) | plan.json@b3e19c0, PR #31 |
| chat: scope cut to 10 days (OBSERVED, internal) | plan: 21 days remain (OBSERVED) | #acme-internal 1962…, docs/effort |

## Coverage
| Tier | Adapter | State | Elapsed | Locators | Newest | Covered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T0 | git | read | 4 s | 31 | 2031-03-14 | origin/main at b3e19c0, 30 days |
| T1 | majordomus | read | 22 s | 17 | 2031-03-09 | context, plan, 0 candidates; handover stale (5 d) |
| T2 | forge CLI | read | 41 s | 63 | 2031-03-13 | 42 open, 18 closed issues, 3 PRs, deploy runs |
| T3 | tracker API | failed | 2 s | 0 | – | 401 unauthenticated; offline export used |
| T4 | chat workspace | partial | 60 s | 24 | 2031-03-14 | 2 channels (1 shared-with-external), 2 DMs; cut at its budget share |
```

The JSON rendering carries the same sections, and every finding carries its `tag` and
`locator`.

examples.title: Picture of a repository without a Majordomus layer
examples.body:
Intent: "What is the state of acme-tools?" The repository has no `.ai/manifest.yaml`.

The worker skips stages 3–5 and records them as one coverage row: "T1: not supervised". It
does not run `majordomus init` and does not suggest running it unasked. The picture rests on
the tree (stage 2) and on whatever forges, trackers and conversations answer (stages 6–9).
Precedence still holds: the tree outranks everything else.

The decisions, open questions and rationale normally read from the `.ai/` layer come here
from ADR-like documents in the tree, issue threads and conversations. Each one is tagged
with that weaker source. Stage 11 proposes no Majordomus records. A missing layer is not
something to fix inside this skill.

skills.title: Bring a branch current by the cheapest safe strategy
skills.description: Decide, from the integration engine's own assessment, whether a branch needs nothing, master merged in, a repair by its owner, a fresh branch from master or to wait, and carry out only that, with every rewrite preceded by a rescue ref and every push a fast-forward.
inputs: one branch or pull request, a train, or the whole open queue, named by number or branch
the last recorded forge observation (`majordomus prs refresh` makes a new one)
a checkout with git history, the peer board and the derived-merge driver configured
outputs: for each candidate, the strategy chosen, the disposition and relation it was chosen from, and the command that carried it out or the reason it was left
a rescue ref for any head that was rewritten, proven on the remote before the rewrite
the head pushed, the run of the required check it started, and the queue read again afterwards

examples.title: A link behind master
examples.body:
Train 13c landed and every open pull request went `CONFLICTING` on the forge within minutes.
Bring the next train's members current without spending a check run on any head that does
not need one: refresh the observation, read each member's disposition and relation, merge
master into the `needs_refresh` ones whose conflicts are only derived files with
`prs repair <n> --apply`, leave the heads that already contain master alone, hand the one
`conflicting` member back to its owner naming its authored files, and wait for the stacked
link until its base lands. Report each member with the strategy, the head pushed and the
check run it started.

skills.title: Repository review
skills.description: An evidence-driven review of the actual state of the repository, or of one change to it, before meaningful engineering work is recommended or done.
inputs: a checkout of the repository with git history available
the scope under review, or the whole repository when none is given
the effective context for every path in scope (majordomus context resolve <path>)
outputs: findings, each with severity, evidence, location, the smallest correct fix and the evidence that would prove it
the list of what was checked, including the areas where nothing was found

examples.title: Review a subsystem
examples.body:
Review one directory and the documents that describe it, whether or not anything in it
changed recently. Scope is the directory; the report names the documents it was checked
against.

```text
Apply the repo-review skill to lib/knowledge.sh, lib/knowledge.awk and docs/CLI.md's
knowledge section. Question: does the documented behaviour match the implementation,
and is every documented behaviour covered by a case under test/cases/?
```

examples.title: Review an implementation against its issue
examples.body:
Review a branch against the issue it claims to complete: the acceptance criteria, the
declared paths, and the evidence the issue requires.

```text
Apply the repo-review skill to branch feature/x against issue I0042
(majordomus plan show I0042). For each acceptance criterion, name the test that proves it
or report that none does. Report any file the branch touched outside the issue's paths.
```

examples.title: Review the current diff
examples.body:
Review the working tree and the staged changes against the base branch before they are
committed. Scope is the diff; everything else is read for context and not reviewed.

```text
Apply the repo-review skill to the current diff against master.
Scope: the files changed in the worktree. Report FAIL findings first.
```

examples.title: Review generated files and documents for drift
examples.body:
Review whether every generated surface matches its canonical source right now, by
running the repository's own drift checks and reading what they do not cover.

```text
Apply the repo-review skill to the generated surfaces: run scripts/generate-site-data
--check and majordomus generate --check, then read the documents under docs/ that
describe behaviour and compare them with the commands they describe. Report every
claim a document makes that no check or test would catch if it became false.
```

examples.title: Review the whole repository's architecture
examples.body:
Review the repository against the boundaries it declares: canonical sources, generated
projections, provider neutrality, and the rules that are enforced by a reviewer only.

```text
Apply the repo-review skill to the whole repository. Concentrate on sections 3 and 5 of
the procedure: every generated artifact and the check that fails when it is stale, and
every declared boundary and the code that keeps it. List the rules that are not
machine-enforced and say for each whether the tree honours it today.
```

skills.title: Report by verification state
skills.description: Write the outcome of a piece of work as claims each marked VERIFIED, PARTIAL or BLOCKED by the evidence actually observed, so a reader can tell what was proved from what was only done or intended.
inputs: the work as it stands in the tree, with its commits and anything pushed
the commands that ran during the work, with their exit codes and the relevant output
outputs: a report whose every claim carries one of VERIFIED, PARTIAL or BLOCKED and the evidence for it
the gaps, each with the command or decision that would close it

examples.title: Final report of a task
examples.body:
A task is closing and its report will be read by someone deciding whether to merge.

```text
Apply the report-verification-state skill to this task's outcome. One claim per line, each
marked VERIFIED, PARTIAL or BLOCKED with the command and exit code behind it; BLOCKED first,
and one line per gap saying what would close it.
```

claude.name: mj-server
claude.description: Majordomus server: The shared server, and every server of the repository.

claude.name: mj-session-domain
claude.description: Majordomus session domain: What identifies this checkout, and how each store spells it; The episode lifecycle, as data.

claude.name: mj-shell
claude.description: Majordomus shell: Refuse undeclared shell.

claude.name: mj-skills
claude.description: Majordomus skills: One skill, with everything derived about it; Every skill, with its derived standing; What the skills owe and do not have.

claude.name: mj-trace
claude.description: Majordomus trace: What contract this commit served; What realised this issue; The whole work graph above the branch.

claude.name: mj-web
claude.description: Majordomus web: Every web surface, resolved.

claude.name: mj-why
claude.description: Majordomus why: Operational areas; Audiences; Diagnose a selection; The catalogue; One moment; Validate the catalogue.

claude.name: mj-worktree
claude.description: Majordomus worktree: The canonical worktree of a branch, made or found; One branch: where its worktree belongs and what is there; What it would take to bring every worktree home; Where this is, and whether that is where it belongs; The whole topology; How far a checkout is from the remote trunk…

claude.name: assess-before-deleting
claude.description: Remove a file, branch, worktree, record or process only after each candidate has been classified by what depends on it and what would be lost, and the reversible step has been taken first.

claude.name: deploy-site
claude.description: Publish the website to GitHub Pages from a terminal, through the one script the Pages workflow runs, when waiting for the Actions queue is not acceptable.

claude.name: evolve
claude.description: Turn what sessions observed into reviewed knowledge and into the rule, skill, document or test each lesson belongs in, then deliver the change and tell every peer what moved.

claude.name: implement
claude.description: Carry a requested change through the repository evidence-first, from the invariant it must keep to a verified, reconciled, documented and committed tree, without widening its scope.

claude.name: integrator
claude.description: Carry a finished change from an open pull request to master and beyond through the one integration engine and the one landing seat, answering at each stage why it is not there yet and stopping only at a landing verified on master, a release, or a named blocker with its next act.

claude.name: pack-for-chatgpt
claude.description: Turn a committed tree into token-bounded Markdown shards that a ChatGPT project's file search indexes, verified to carry no binary, worktree, link, build output, projection or leaked value, and hand them over with the commit they were cut from.

claude.name: pack-for-review
claude.description: Prepare a bounded, reproducible snapshot of the tracked tree for a reviewer who cannot read the repository directly, with the local half and anything secret left out and the questions the review must answer written down.

claude.name: rebaser
claude.description: Decide, from the integration engine's own assessment, whether a branch needs nothing, master merged in, a repair by its owner, a fresh branch from master or to wait, and carry out only that, with every rewrite preceded by a rescue ref and every push a fast-forward.

claude.name: repo-review
claude.description: An evidence-driven review of the actual state of the repository, or of one change to it, before meaningful engineering work is recommended or done.

claude.name: report-verification-state
claude.description: Write the outcome of a piece of work as claims each marked VERIFIED, PARTIAL or BLOCKED by the evidence actually observed, so a reader can tell what was proved from what was only done or intended.
